slides.texte_overlay:
7 underrated skills that'll make you
dangerously capable in your 20s
Learn to iron a shirt. Collar, cuffs, sleeves, then the body. Ten minutes, once a week. A crisp shirt makes you look put together for interviews, dates and every important day in between.
Learn to read a map without your phone. Know north, know the main roads of your city. When the battery dies or the signal drops, you're the one who still knows exactly where to go.
Learn to write a proper CV. One page, clear results, no fluff. Update it every six months, even when you're happy at work. Opportunities show up fast, and the ready guy gets them.
Learn to fall asleep without a screen. Book, dim light, same time every night. Good sleep is the skill behind every other skill, and most guys in their 20s never learn it.
Learn to host a dinner. One main, one dessert, a playlist, clean glasses. Being able to bring people together at your place is a skill that builds friendships for life.
Learn to learn a little every day. Five minutes of history, art or science adds up to a mind full of ideas by 30. It's the most underrated skill on this list.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: scrolling every night until 1am. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. By 30, your head is full of ideas.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn to say "I need help." To a friend, a colleague, a doctor. Guys who ask early fix problems in a week. Guys who wait until it's a crisis lose months. Asking is a strength.
